tickets.title: Add yourself to the team directory
tickets.summary: The People page has an empty spot reserved for you. Fill it in, on a branch, with a commit message I can respect.
steps: In your real terminal, inside the `the-studio` folder, start from fresh main: `git switch main` then `git pull`
Create your branch: `git switch -c onboarding/add-<your-name>` (lowercase, dashes, no spaces)
Open `src/content/team.ts` and replace `null` in `newHire` with your entry. Save, then check the People page in the app.
Look before you leap: `git status` and `git diff`
Stage and commit: `git add src/content/team.ts` then `git commit -m "..."` with a message that would survive Commit Court
Publish your branch: `git push -u origin onboarding/add-<your-name>`
Switch back to Claude Code, where your coach lives, and type **done**. Stuck? Type **hint**.
acceptance: Your `onboarding/...` branch exists on GitHub
It has a commit that changes only `src/content/team.ts`
The commit message passes Commit Court: imperative, capitalized, no period, 50 characters or fewer
`favoriteToken` is a real token name (Dotty will check, and so will TypeScript)
`main` is untouched. Nobody pushes to main.

tickets.title: Who broke the button?
tickets.summary: Someone hard-coded a hex color into the default Button. Find the exact commit that did it, put the token back, and name the culprit commit in your message.
steps: Start fresh: `git switch main` then `git pull`
See the crime: `npm run dot` (Dotty's audit fails on main right now)
Investigate: `git log --oneline -- src/components/ui/button.tsx`, then `git show <hash>` or `git blame src/components/ui/button.tsx`
Branch: `git switch -c fix/button-color`
In `src/components/ui/button.tsx`, put the default variant back to `bg-primary` and `hover:bg-primary/90`. Run `npm run dot` until it passes.
Commit with a body that names the culprit: `git commit -am "Restore primary token on default Button" -m "Introduced in <hash>."`
Push: `git push -u origin fix/button-color`
Switch back to Claude Code (your coach) and type **done**.
acceptance: A `fix/...` branch is on GitHub
It changes only `src/components/ui/button.tsx`
`npm run dot` passes on your branch
Your commit message includes the short hash of the commit that broke it
Your subject line passes Commit Court

tickets.title: Your first pull requests
tickets.summary: Two branches, two pull requests. Merge your Button fix as a warm-up. Then open one for your directory entry. I will request a change. You will make it.
steps: Start fresh: `git switch main` then `git pull`
On GitHub, open **your** repo → **Pull requests** → **New pull request**. Base: `main`. Compare: `fix/button-color`. Create it, then click **Merge pull request**.
Open a second pull request: base `main`, compare `onboarding/add-<your-name>`. Read Gus's review in his DM in the app.
Make Gus's change on that branch: `git switch onboarding/add-<your-name>`, then `git merge main` to bring in Priya's new `pronouns` field.
Add `pronouns` to your entry in `src/content/team.ts`. Commit it. `git push`. Watch the pull request update itself.
Merge the second pull request on GitHub.
Back home: `git switch main`, `git pull`, then tidy up with `git branch -d fix/button-color`
Switch back to Claude Code (your coach) and type **done**.
acceptance: Your Button fix is merged into `main` (the build goes green)
Your directory entry is merged into `main`
Your entry has `pronouns`, the change Gus requested
You merged `main` into your branch before adding it
Everything reached `main` through pull requests, not direct pushes

tickets.title: Rename the People page
tickets.summary: Rename the People page to "Team" with the subtitle "Who's who at The Studio". Bjorn changed the same lines on his own branch. Merge his branch into yours and resolve it: **your title, his subtitle**.
steps: Start fresh: `git switch main` then `git pull`
Branch: `git switch -c copy/people-page`
In `src/content/copy.ts`, set `title` to `'Team'` and `subtitle` to `"Who's who at The Studio"`. Commit.
Bring in Bjorn's work: `git merge origin/bjorn/people-page-copy`. Git will stop with a **CONFLICT**. That's the boss.
`git status` shows the conflicted file. Open it. Keep **your title** and **Bjorn's subtitle**. Delete all three marker lines (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`).
Tell git it's resolved: `git add src/content/copy.ts`, then `git commit` (the message is pre-written; save and close).
Run `npm run check`, then `git push -u origin copy/people-page`
Open a pull request and merge it. Then `git switch main` and `git pull`.
Switch back to Claude Code (your coach) and type **done**.
acceptance: Bjorn's branch is merged into `main`
The title is yours ("Team")
The subtitle is Bjorn's
No conflict markers anywhere
It reached `main` through a pull request

tickets.title: Ship one fix from a half-done branch
tickets.summary: There's a typo on the People page ("quater"). Bjorn already fixed it, on a branch full of half-done header experiments. Ship **only** his fix, today, without his experiments.
steps: Pretend you're mid-task: change any line in `src/content/copy.ts` and don't commit it.
Priya interrupts. Park your edit: `git stash`. (`git status` is clean now.)
Start fresh: `git switch main` then `git pull`
Find Bjorn's fix: `git log --oneline origin/bjorn/header-redesign`. You want the typo commit, nothing else.
Branch: `git switch -c hotfix/people-footer-typo`
Copy just that commit: `git cherry-pick <hash>`
Push, open a pull request, merge it. Then `git switch main` and `git pull`.
Bring your parked edit back: `git stash pop`. (Then throw it away with `git restore src/content/copy.ts`. It was pretend.)
Switch back to Claude Code (your coach) and type **done**.
acceptance: The typo is fixed on `main`
None of Bjorn's header experiments reached `main`
A `hotfix/...` branch carries Bjorn's fix as a cherry-pick
It reached `main` through a pull request

tickets.title: Friday outage
tickets.summary: Bjorn deployed "fun Friday colors" to main. The app is orange and green. Gus pushed something good right after. Undo **only** Bjorn's commit, without rewriting history.
steps: Start fresh: `git switch main` then `git pull`. (Yes, the app looks like that now.)
Find the bad commit: `git log --oneline -- src/styles/tokens.css`
Branch: `git switch -c revert/friday-theme`
Undo it safely: `git revert <hash>`. Save the pre-written message and close the editor.
Check the colors are back in the app, run `npm run check`, then `git push -u origin revert/friday-theme`
Open a pull request and merge it. `git switch main`, `git pull`.
Switch back to Claude Code (your coach) and type **done**.
Do **not** use `git reset --hard` or `git push --force` on main. Gus will know.
acceptance: `tokens.css` on `main` matches how it was before Bjorn's commit
Gus's later commit is still on `main`
